title: Stop the workshops from overfilling, whichever way attendees arrive

blocks.text: The conference sells seats in its hands-on workshops in two ways: attendees sign up on the website, and badges sold by a partner ticketing system are imported in batches. Both run on many threads at once, and the venue's rule decides how many people a room admits. Last year two workshops ended up with more attendees than chairs, and the import was blamed in one case and the sign-up page in the other.

Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/Workshops.java`, `tryEnroll(...)`, and change anything else in the file you need to. When you're done, no workshop gets more attendees than the venue's rule admits, whether they arrive through the sign-up page, the import, or both at the same moment. Staff at the door can still add walk-ins over capacity. About six lines in total.
The tests use a venue whose rule can hold its first answer back, so that a second attendee arrives while the first is still being decided.

cases.says: sign-ups take seats until the venue's rule refuses, and each workshop counts its own
imported badges and sign-ups fill the same seats, and a walk-in can still be added over capacity
two sign-ups at once for the last seat: one gets it and the other is refused
two imported badges at once for the last seat: one gets it and the other is refused
an imported badge and a sign-up at once for the last seat: one gets it and the other is refused

origin.section: A Fix Made in the Owning Class Reaches Every Caller Without Touching Them

concepts: When a validate-then-update sequence is copied into several callers, making one copy atomic leaves the other copies racing, with each other and beside the fixed one, while the fixed copy's own load test passes.

With the validate-then-update as one method of the owning class, one edit to that method fixes every caller, mixed traffic included, without changing the callers, and a load test of that method covers them all.
